model_explanation: "only gave Ellen grapes" entails that no one besides Ellen got grapes, so Tom did not get grapes.
"only gave Ellen apples" implies Ellen received apples and no other things from Sam, so she did not receive oranges.
"only gave Rob grapes" means Rob is the sole recipient of grapes; saying Sam also gave Ellen grapes contradicts this.
"only gave Rob apples" makes Rob the sole recipient of apples; saying Sam also gave Ellen apples contradicts this.
"only gave Ellen apples" entails that Ellen is the only recipient of apples, so Bill did not get apples.
"only gave Rob apples" entails that Rob is the only recipient of apples, so Sue did not get apples.
"only gave Rob oranges" restricts what Rob got (only oranges), but says nothing about whether Rob got other kinds of things like apples; it does not entail or contradict that he also got apples.

"only gave Rob apples" restricts what Rob got (only apples) but not who got what; it does not by itself entail or contradict that he also got grapes (the statement is about recipient, not object set).
"only gave Rob bananas" entails Rob is the sole recipient of bananas, so Ellen did not get bananas.
"only gave Mary apples" entails Mary is the only recipient of apples; saying Sam also gave Ellen apples contradicts this.
